L16: ## 15.53 Excellent rings
L17: 
L18: In this section we discuss Grothendieck's notion of excellent rings. For the definitions of G-rings, J-2 rings, and universally catenary rings we refer to Definition 【11†15.51.1】, Definition 【12†15.48.1】, and Algebra, Definition 【13†10.105.3】.
L19: 
L20: 【14†Definition 15.53.1.】 Let $R$ be a ring.
L21: 
L22:   1. We say $R$ is quasi-excellent if $R$ is Noetherian, a G-ring, and J-2.
L23: 
L24:   2. We say $R$ is excellent if $R$ is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.
L25: Thus a Noetherian ring is quasi-excellent if it has geometrically regular formal fibres and if any finite type algebra over it has closed singular set. For such a ring to be excellent we require in addition that there exists (locally) a good dimension function. We will see later (Section 【15†15.111】) that to be universally catenary can be formulated as a condition on the maps $R_\mathfrak m \to R_\mathfrak m^\wedge $ for maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$ of $R$.
L26: 【16†Lemma 15.53.2.】 Any localization of a finite type ring over a (quasi-)excellent ring is (quasi-)excellent.
L27: 
L28: Proof. For finite type algebras this follows from the definitions for the properties J-2 and universally catenary. For G-rings, see Proposition 【17†15.51.10】. We omit the proof that localization preserves (quasi-)excellency. $\square$
L29: 
L30: 【18†Proposition 15.53.3.】 The following types of rings are excellent:
L31: 
L32:   1. fields,
L33: 
L34:   2. Noetherian complete local rings,
L35: 
L36:   3. $\mathbf{Z}$,
L37:   4. Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero,
L38: 
L39:   5. finite type ring extensions of any of the above.
L40: Proof. See Propositions 【19†15.51.12】 and 【20†15.49.7】 to see that these rings are G-rings and have J-2. Any Cohen-Macaulay ring is universally catenary, see Algebra, Lemma 【21†10.105.9】. In particular fields, Dedekind rings, and more generally regular rings are universally catenary. Via the Cohen structure theorem we see that complete local rings are universally catenary, see Algebra, Remark 【22†10.160.9】. $\square$
L41: 
L42: The material developed above has some consequences for Nagata rings.
L43: 【23†Lemma 15.53.4.】 Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent
L44: 
L45:   1. $A$ is Nagata, and
L46: 
L47:   2. the formal fibres of $A$ are geometrically reduced.
L48: Proof. Assume (2). By Algebra, Lemma 【24†10.162.14】 we have to show that if $A \to B$ is finite, $B$ is a domain, and $\mathfrak m' \subset B$ is a maximal ideal, then $B_{\mathfrak m'}$ is analytically unramified. Combining Lemmas 【25†15.52.9】 and 【26†15.52.4】 and Proposition 【27†15.52.5】 we see that the formal fibres of $B_{\mathfrak m'}$ are geometrically reduced. In particular $B_{\mathfrak m'}^\wedge \otimes _ B L$ is reduced where $L$ is the fraction field of $B$.
L49: It follows that $B_{\mathfrak m'}^\wedge $ is reduced, i.e., $B_{\mathfrak m'}$ is analytically unramified.
L50: Assume (1). Let $\mathfrak q \subset A$ be a prime ideal and let $K/\kappa (\mathfrak q)$ be a finite extension. We have to show that $A^\wedge \otimes _ A K$ is reduced. Let $A/\mathfrak q \subset B \subset K$ be a local subring finite over $A$ whose fraction field is $K$.
L51: To construct $B$ choose $x_1, \ldots , x_ n \in K$ which generate $K$ over $\kappa (\mathfrak q)$ and which satisfy monic polynomials $P_ i(T) = T^{d_ i} + a_{i, 1} T^{d_ i - 1} + \ldots + a_{i, d_ i} = 0$ with $a_{i, j} \in \mathfrak m$. Then let $B$ be the $A$-subalgebra of $K$ generated by $x_1, \ldots , x_ n$. (For more details see the proof of Algebra, Lemma 【24†10.162.14】.) Then
L52: \[ A^\wedge \otimes _ A K = (A^\wedge \otimes _ A B)_\mathfrak q = B^\wedge _\mathfrak q \]
L53: 
L54: Since $B^\wedge $ is reduced by Algebra, Lemma 【24†10.162.14】 the proof is complete. $\square$
L55: 
L56: 【28†Lemma 15.53.5.】 A quasi-excellent ring is Nagata.
L57: Proof. Let $R$ be quasi-excellent. Using that a finite type algebra over $R$ is quasi-excellent (Lemma 【16†15.53.2】) we see that it suffices to show that any quasi-excellent domain is N-1, see Algebra, Lemma 【29†10.162.3】. Applying Algebra, Lemma 【30†10.161.15】 (and using that a quasi-excellent ring is J-2) we reduce to showing that a quasi-excellent local domain $R$ is N-1. As $R \to R^\wedge $ is regular we see that $R^\wedge $ is reduced by Lemma 【31†15.43.1】.
L58: In other words, $R$ is analytically unramified. Hence $R$ is N-1 by Algebra, Lemma 【32†10.162.10】. $\square$
L59: 【33†Lemma 15.53.6.】 Let $(A, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring. If $A$ is normal and the formal fibres of $A$ are normal (for example if $A$ is excellent or quasi-excellent), then $A^\wedge $ is normal.
L60: 
L61: Proof. Follows immediately from Algebra, Lemma 【34†10.163.8】. $\square$

L23: 【8†Lemma 15.111.4.】 Let $A$ be a formally catenary Noetherian local ring. Then $A$ is universally catenary.
L24: Proof. We may replace $A$ by $A/\mathfrak p$ where $\mathfrak p$ is a minimal prime of $A$, see Algebra, Lemma 【15†10.105.8】. Thus we may assume that the spectrum of $A^\wedge $ is equidimensional. It suffices to show that every local ring essentially of finite type over $A$ is catenary (see for example Algebra, Lemma 【16†10.105.6】).
L25: Hence it suffices to show that $A[x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_\mathfrak m$ is catenary where $\mathfrak m \subset A[x_1, \ldots , x_ n]$ is a maximal ideal lying over $\mathfrak m_ A$, see Algebra, Lemma 【17†10.54.5】 (and Algebra, Lemmas 【18†10.105.7】 and 【19†10.105.4】). Let $\mathfrak m' \subset A^\wedge [x_1, \ldots , x_ n]$ be the unique maximal ideal lying over $\mathfrak m$. Then
L26: \[ A[x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_\mathfrak m \to A^\wedge [x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_{\mathfrak m'} \]
L27: is local and flat (Algebra, Lemma 【20†10.97.2】). Hence it suffices to show that the ring on the right hand side catenary with equidimensional spectrum, see Lemma 【10†15.111.3】. It is catenary because complete local rings are universally catenary (Algebra, Remark 【21†10.160.9】). Pick any minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A^\wedge [x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_{\mathfrak m'}$.
L28: Then $\mathfrak q = \mathfrak p A^\wedge [x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_{\mathfrak m'}$ for some minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A^\wedge $ (small detail omitted). Hence
L29: \[ \dim (A^\wedge [x_1, \ldots , x_ n]_{\mathfrak m'}/\mathfrak q) = \dim (A^\wedge /\mathfrak p) + n = \dim (A^\wedge ) + n \]
L30: 
L31: the first equality by Algebra, Lemma 【22†10.112.7】 and the second because the spectrum of $A^\wedge $ is equidimensional. This finishes the proof. $\square$
